en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 3.11.
Upādānagocchaka, Kusalattika (Wholesome Triplet)
3.11.1.1–7. Section on “Dependent on” Etc. (Paṭiccādivāra).
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka).
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not accompanied by clinging (noupādāna), a wholesome state not accompanied by clinging arises by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya). (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, one; in the case of the object condition, one … pe … in the case of the non-disappearance condition, one. (Abbreviated.
(In the co-nascence section … pe … and in the inquiry section, it is one in every instance.
Dependent on a state associated with clinging that is unwholesome, there arises a state associated with clinging that is unwholesome by way of the root condition. Clinging … [and so forth].
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not associated with clinging (*noupādāna*), an unwholesome state not associated with clinging arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with clinging (*upādāna*), both unwholesome states associated with clinging and unwholesome states not associated with clinging arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state not associated with clinging, an unwholesome state not associated with clinging arises by way of root condition... [three].

Dependent on unwholesome states that are both with-clinging (*sopādāna*) and unwholesome states that are without-clinging (*anupādāna*), an unwholesome state that is with-clinging arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). ... [Three] (Abbreviated). Under root-condition there are nine;
under object-condition there are nine (nine in all cases); under non-disappearance-condition there are nine. (Abbreviated).
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is without-clinging, an unwholesome state that is without-clinging arises by way of non-root-condition. (Abbreviated).

In the absence of root-condition (na-hetu): one; in the absence of predominance-condition (na-adhipati): nine; in the absence of prenascence-condition (na-purejāta): nine ... pe ... in the absence of kamma-condition (na-kamma): three; in the absence of result-condition (na-vipāka): nine; in the absence of dissociation-condition (na-vippayutta): nine.
An unwholesome state associated with clinging (upādāna) is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state associated with clinging.

(Abbreviated. In the presence of root-condition (hetu): nine; in the presence of object-condition (ārammaṇa): nine; in the presence of predominance-condition (adhipati): nine (in the section not based on clinging-roots [noupādānamūlaka], there are three, including co-nascent predominance).

In the immediate condition, nine; ... [and so on] ... in the dependence condition, nine; in the decisive support condition, nine; in the repetition condition, nine; in the kamma condition, three (without the root of clinging);

in the nutriment condition, three; in the faculty condition, three; in the jhāna condition, three; in the path condition, nine; in the association condition, nine; in the presence condition, nine; ... [and so on] ...
in the non-disappearance condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)
Dependent on a non-clinging indeterminate state, a non-clinging indeterminate state arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root-condition there is one; under object-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there is one. (Abbreviated.
(In the “Conascent” chapter … pe … and in the “Investigation” chapter, there is one in every instance.)
3.11.2.1. Section on the Wholesome (Kusalapada), Wholesome Triplet (Kusalattika):
Dependent on a wholesome state that is subject to clinging, a wholesome state subject to clinging arises by way of the root-condition (hetu-paccaya).
Dependent on a wholesome state not subject to clinging, a wholesome state not subject to clinging arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. There are two under root; two under object; ... [and so on] ... two under non-disappearance.
Dependent on an unwholesome state subject to clinging, an unwholesome state subject to clinging arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, one; in the case of the object condition, one ... pe ... in the case of the non-disappearance condition, one.
(Abbreviated. (In the section on co-nascence as well ... pe ... in the section on inquiry as well, it is one in every instance.
Dependent on a state that is both subject to clinging and indeterminate, there arises a state that is subject to clinging and indeterminate by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not subject to clinging and is indeterminate, there arises a state that is not subject to clinging and is indeterminate, by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is not subject to clinging and is indeterminate, there arises a state that is subject to clinging and is indeterminate, by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is not subject to clinging and is indeterminate, there arise states both subject to clinging and not subject to clinging, and indeterminate, by way of root-condition.
And states arise by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is both subject to clinging and indeterminate, and a state that is not subject to clinging and indeterminate, a state that is subject to clinging and indeterminate arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are five;
under object condition, two ... pe ... under repetition condition, one ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition, five.
3.11.3. The Pair on Association with Grasping (Upādānasampayuttaduka), The Triplet on the Wholesome (Kusalattika):
Root Condition (Hetu). Dependent on a wholesome state dissociated from grasping, a wholesome state dissociated from grasping arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the root condition, one; in the object condition, one … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, one. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] in the co-nascent section … pe … and in the inquiry section, it is one in every instance.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with clinging, an unwholesome state associated with clinging arises by way of the root condition … three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state dissociated from clinging, an unwholesome state dissociated from clinging arises by way of root condition … two.
Dependent on both an unwholesome state associated with clinging and an unwholesome state dissociated from clinging, an unwholesome state associated with clinging arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root there are six; under object there are six (six in all cases); under non-disappearance there are six. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to not-root: one; with respect to not-predominance: six ... [etc. ... with respect to not-kamma: four; with respect to not-resultant: six; with respect to not-dissociation: six.
An unwholesome state associated with clinging is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state associated with clinging ... three.
An unwholesome state dissociated from clinging is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state dissociated from clinging ... two.

Unwholesome states associated with clinging and unwholesome states dissociated from clinging are related to a state associated with clinging that is unwholesome by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated. There are six [conditions] in the case of the root-condition; nine in the case of the object-condition;
nine in the case of the predominance-condition (three based on those associated with clinging: conascence-predominance; one for those dissociated from clinging);
nine in the case of the proximity-condition; nine in the case of the contiguity-condition; six in the case of the conascence-condition; [six] in the case of the mutuality-condition...
Six for dependence, six for strong-dependence, nine for repetition, four for kamma, four for nutriment,
four for faculty, four for jhāna, four for path, six for association, six for presence, nine for absence,
nine for disappearance, and six for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
Dependent on a state that is dissociated from clinging and indeterminate, there arises a state dissociated from clinging and indeterminate by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root, one; under object, one … pe … under non-disappearance, one. (Abbreviated.
(In the section on co-nascence … pe … and in the section on inquiry, it is one in every instance.)
3.11.4. The Dyad of Grasping and the Graspable; The Triplet of the Wholesome;

The Root Condition. Dependent on a wholesome state that is both graspable and not itself grasping, there arises a wholesome state that is graspable and not itself grasping, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, one; in the object condition, one … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, one. (Abbreviated.
(In the co-nascent section … pe … and in the inquiry section, it is one in every instance.

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both a clinging and subject to clinging, there arises an unwholesome state that is both a clinging and subject to clinging by way of the root condition … three.

Dependent on a state that is both subject to clinging and not itself clinging, and is unwholesome, there arises a state that is both subject to clinging and not itself clinging, and is unwholesome, by way of root condition ... three.

Dependent on a state that is both clinging and subject to clinging and is unwholesome, and a state that is both subject to clinging and not itself clinging and is unwholesome, there arises a state that is both clinging and subject to clinging and is unwholesome, by way of root condition ...
three. (Abbreviated. Nine for root; nine for object ... pe ... nine for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a neutral state that is both subject to clinging and not itself clinging, there arises a neutral state that is both subject to clinging and not itself clinging, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root-condition there is one; under object-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there is one. (Abbreviated.
(In the section on co-nascence as well … pe … and in the section on inquiry as well, there is one in every instance.)
3.11.5. The Pair on Grasping and Being Associated with Grasping; The Triplet on the Wholesome;

The Root Condition. Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both grasping and associated with grasping, there arises an unwholesome state that is both grasping and associated with grasping by way of the root condition... [three].

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is associated with clinging but is not itself clinging, there arises an unwholesome state associated with clinging but not itself clinging, by way of root condition ... [three].

Dependent on a state that is both clinging and associated with clinging and is unwholesome, and a state that is associated with clinging but not itself clinging and is unwholesome, there arises a state that is both clinging and associated with clinging and is unwholesome.
Conditioned by root: three. (Abbreviated.
Under root there are nine; under object, nine; under predominance, nine ... pe ... under non-disappearance, nine. (Abbreviated.
(This method is similar to the unwholesome section of the *upādāna-duka*. However, here, under the condition of root, this is the difference. Also in the "conascent" chapter...)
…pe… (In the section on questions as well, there are nine in all.
3.11.6. The Dyad of Dissociated from Clinging but Subject to Clinging; The Triplet of the Wholesome;
The Root.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from clinging but subject to clinging, there arises a wholesome state dissociated from clinging and subject to clinging by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state dissociated from clinging and not subject to clinging, there arises a wholesome state dissociated from clinging and not subject to clinging by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are two under root, two under object ... pe ... two under non-disappearance.

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is dissociated from clinging but subject to clinging, there arises an unwholesome state dissociated from clinging but subject to clinging, by way of root condition. (In all cases, one.

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is dissociated from clinging but subject to clinging, there arises an indeterminate state dissociated from clinging but subject to clinging, by way of root condition.

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is dissociated from clinging and not subject to clinging, there arises an indeterminate state dissociated from clinging and not subject to clinging, by way of root condition. … three.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from clinging, subject to clinging, and indeterminate, and dependent on a state that is dissociated from clinging, not subject to clinging, and indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from clinging, subject to clinging, and indeterminate, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are five under root, two under object … pe … five under non-disappearance.
The Triplet on the Wholesome within the Group on Grasping is finished.
